applicantVariants.label: Under 21 (GDL: special learner's or examination permit)

retake.waitBetweenAttempts: Must reschedule; typically at least the next available day
retake.retakeFee: Retest fee applies for the knowledge test

gdl.permitMinAge: 16 (special learner's permit, with approved driver ed) / 17 (examination permit)
gdl.supervisedHoursRequired: 50 hours (permit holders under 21, permit issued on/after Feb 1, 2025)
gdl.nightCurfew: No driving 11:01 p.m.-5 a.m. (GDL permit and probationary drivers)
gdl.passengerLimits: One passenger, unless accompanied by a parent/guardian or the passengers are the driver's dependents

requiredDocuments: Proof of identity and age meeting the MVC 6 Points of ID standard
Social Security Number (or proof of ineligibility)
Proof of New Jersey residential address
process.realIdNotes: New Jersey issues both REAL ID and Standard licenses. REAL ID requires documents that satisfy the 6 Points of ID plus proof of Social Security Number and address; needed to board domestic flights after the federal deadline.
process.visionStandard: 20/50 or better in at least one eye, with or without corrective lenses

facts.pointSuspensionThreshold: 12 or more points results in license suspension
facts.moveOverRule: Move over one lane or slow down for stopped emergency, tow, and highway maintenance vehicles displaying flashing lights
facts.interstateMaxSpeed: 65 mph (where posted, including the Turnpike and Garden State Parkway)

bacAdult.display: A person may not operate a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08% or more, or while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs.

citation.label: “Florence's Law”, lowering the per se limit to 0.08%, approved and effective January 20, 2004

conditions.detail: drivers under the legal drinking age of 21

bacUnder21.display: A person under 21 who drives with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.01% or more but less than 0.08% forfeits driving privileges for 30 to 90 days plus community service and an alcohol program.

citation.label: Underage drinking and driving (P.L.1992, c.189), as amended by P.L.2003, c.314, approved and effective January 20, 2004

bacCommercial.display: A person may not operate a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04% or more, or while under the influence of a controlled substance.

citation.label: Alcohol, controlled substance use prohibited (commercial drivers); L.1990, c.103, s.5

state.reason: New Jersey does not impose a fixed-length license suspension for a first chemical test refusal. Under N.J.S.A. 39:4-50.4a(a)(1), as amended by P.L.2019, c.248, a first refusal forfeits driving privileges only until the person installs an ignition interlock device; a second refusal adds one to two years after installation and a third adds eight years. Refusal is a motor vehicle offense, not a crime.

impliedConsentRefusal.display: First refusal: loss of driving privileges until an ignition interlock device is installed (interlock then required); second refusal: one to two years after installation; third: eight years. Refusal is a motor vehicle offense, not a criminal offense.

citation.label: Refusal to submit to test; penalties, as amended by P.L.2019, c.248 (effective the first day of the fourth month after the August 23, 2019 approval)

openContainerProhibited.display: It is unlawful to have an open or unsealed container of an alcoholic beverage in the passenger compartment of a motor vehicle on a public highway or right-of-way, or to consume alcohol while operating one.

citation.label: Consumption of alcoholic beverage in motor vehicle; possession of open container, enacted by P.L.2000, c.83 (approved and, as to this section, effective August 14, 2000)

state.reason: New Jersey no longer sets a fixed first-offense suspension in days. Under N.J.S.A. 39:4-50(a)(1), as amended by P.L.2019, c.248, a first offender with a BAC of 0.08% to under 0.15% forfeits driving privileges only until an ignition interlock device is installed (interlock required three months for BAC under 0.10%, seven months to one year for 0.10% to under 0.15%); a BAC of 0.15% or more brings a four-to-six month forfeiture followed by interlock, and a drug-related first offense brings a seven-month to one-year forfeiture.

duiFirstSuspensionDays.display: No fixed first-offense suspension: for a BAC of 0.08% to under 0.15% the driver loses driving privileges only until an ignition interlock device is installed, with the interlock required for three months to one year depending on BAC; a BAC of 0.15% or more adds a four-to-six month forfeiture.

citation.label: Driving while intoxicated; penalties, as amended by P.L.2019, c.248 (effective the first day of the fourth month after the August 23, 2019 approval)

conditions.detail: interstate and other highways designated under the Sixty-Five MPH Speed Limit Implementation Act and posted at 65 mph

ruralInterstateMaxMph.display: The statutory maximum is 50 mph except where the Commissioner of Transportation designates a 65 mph limit under the Sixty-Five MPH Speed Limit Implementation Act; 65 mph is the highest posted limit on New Jersey interstates.

citation.label: Sixty-Five MPH Speed Limit Implementation Act (L.1997, c.415, s.4)

conditions.detail: urban interstate segments, which are posted no higher than 55 mph

urbanInterstateMaxMph.display: Maximum posted speed limit on urban interstates is 55 mph (65 mph designations apply to rural and limited-access segments).

citation.label: IIHS maximum posted speed limits by state (July 2026)
citation.citation: IIHS, Maximum posted speed limits (New Jersey: 65 mph rural interstates, 55 mph urban interstates)

conditions.detail: any suburban business or residential district

residentialDefaultMph.display: Prima facie lawful speeds: 25 mph in a business or residential district, 35 mph in a suburban business or residential district, and 50 mph elsewhere unless posted otherwise.

citation.label: Rates of speed, as amended by P.L.2019, c.5 (approved and effective January 31, 2019)

conditions.detail: during recess, while children are going to or leaving school at opening or closing hours
when the presence of children is clearly visible from the roadway

schoolZoneMph.display: 25 mph when passing through a school zone during recess, when children are clearly visible from the roadway, or while children are going to or leaving school during opening or closing hours.

citation.label: Rates of speed, as amended by P.L.2019, c.5 (approved and effective January 31, 2019)

basicSpeedLaw.display: Posted and statutory limits are only prima facie lawful and are subject to the careless- and reckless-driving statutes, so a driver must always reduce speed to what is reasonable and safe for conditions.

citation.label: Rates of speed, as amended by P.L.2019, c.5 (approved and effective January 31, 2019)

rightTurnOnRed.display: After stopping at a steady red signal, a driver may turn right unless a sign prohibits the turn, and must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

citation.label: Turns at intersections; right turn on red, as amended by P.L.2009, c.319 (effective the first day of the third month after the January 18, 2010 approval)

leftTurnOnRedFromOneWay.display: New Jersey authorizes only a right turn on red; left turns on a steady red signal, including from a one-way street, are not permitted.

citation.label: Turns at intersections; right turn on red, as amended by P.L.2009, c.319 (effective the first day of the third month after the January 18, 2010 approval)

conditions.detail: front-seat occupants and all occupants under 18

seatBeltEnforcement.display: Primary enforcement for the driver, front-seat passengers and every occupant under 18; for rear-seat occupants 18 and older the belt violation is secondary (enforced only after another stop).

citation.label: Passenger Automobile Seat Belt Usage Act, as amended by P.L.2015, c.50 (effective the first day of the fourth month next following the May 7, 2015 approval)

handheldPhone.display: Use of a hand-held wireless telephone while driving is prohibited for all drivers; only hands-free use is allowed, and drivers holding a permit or probationary license may not use any device.

citation.label: Use of wireless telephones and electronic communication devices, as amended by P.L.2013, c.70 (effective the first day of the 13th month following the June 27, 2013 approval)

texting.display: No driver may use a hand-held wireless electronic communication device to send or receive text or other electronic messages while driving.

citation.label: Use of wireless telephones and electronic communication devices, as amended by P.L.2013, c.70 (effective the first day of the 13th month following the June 27, 2013 approval)

moveOver.display: Approaching a stationary emergency, tow, highway maintenance, utility or other vehicle displaying flashing lights, a driver must change lanes into an available lane away from it or, if a lane change is unsafe, slow below the posted limit and be prepared to stop.

citation.label: Approaching stationary vehicles; move over, as amended by P.L.2025, c.248 (approved and effective January 12, 2026)

headlightsRequired.display: Lighted lamps are required from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, whenever precipitation requires the use of windshield wipers, and whenever fog, smoke or other conditions limit visibility to under 500 feet.

citation.label: Definitions relative to illuminating devices — "when lighted lamps are required" (as amended by P.L.1995, c.305)

parkFtFromHydrant.display: No standing or parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

citation.label: Places where parking prohibited, as amended by P.L.2025, c.155 (approved and effective November 13, 2025)

conditions.detail: ordinary crosswalks and intersecting street side lines
crosswalks where a curb extension or bulbout has been constructed

parkFtFromCrosswalk.display: No parking within 25 feet of the nearest crosswalk or side line of an intersecting street, reduced to 10 feet where a curb extension or bulbout has been built at that crosswalk; parking on a crosswalk is prohibited outright.

citation.label: Places where parking prohibited, as amended by P.L.2025, c.155 (approved and effective November 13, 2025)

parkFtFromStopSign.display: No parking within 50 feet of a stop sign.

citation.label: Places where parking prohibited, as amended by P.L.2025, c.155 (approved and effective November 13, 2025)

parkFtFromRailroad.display: No parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

citation.label: Places where parking prohibited, as amended by P.L.2025, c.155 (approved and effective November 13, 2025)

pointSystem.display: The Motor Vehicle Commission assigns points for moving violations, imposes surcharges and suspends driving privileges on point accumulation.

citation.label: New Jersey MVC, Driving Privilege and Penalties — point system and suspensions
citation.citation: NJ MVC suspension and point system guidance (N.J.S.A. 39:5-30.5; N.J.A.C. 13:19-10.1)

pointSuspension.display: A driver whose current record reaches 12 or more points has driving privileges suspended; there is no look-back window for the suspension threshold (the separate surcharge is triggered by six or more points within three years).

citation.label: New Jersey MVC, Driving Privilege and Penalties — point system and suspensions
citation.citation: NJ MVC suspension and point system guidance (N.J.S.A. 39:5-30.5; N.J.A.C. 13:19-10.1)

permitMinAgeMonths.display: A special learner’s permit may be issued at 16 to a student enrolled in an approved behind-the-wheel driver education course; an examination permit requires age 17.

citation.label: Special learner's permit, as amended by P.L.2021, c.139 (approved and effective June 30, 2021)

permitHoldingMonths.display: The permit must be held and validated for six months of supervised driving before the road test and probationary license.

citation.label: Examination permits and special learner's permits, as amended by P.L.2023, c.216 (effective the first day of the 13th month after the January 8, 2024 approval)

supervisedHoursTotal.display: A permit holder under 21 must complete a minimum of 50 hours of practice driving, certified by the supervising parent, guardian or accompanying driver, before a probationary license is issued.

citation.label: Examination permits and special learner's permits, as amended by P.L.2023, c.216 (effective the first day of the 13th month after the January 8, 2024 approval)

supervisedHoursNight.display: At least 10 of the 50 required practice-driving hours must be completed during hours of darkness.

citation.label: Examination permits and special learner's permits, as amended by P.L.2023, c.216 (effective the first day of the 13th month after the January 8, 2024 approval)

conditions.detail: permit and probationary licence holders under 21

gdlNightCurfew.display: Permit and probationary license holders under 21 may not drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m., except for a documented emergency or bona fide employment or religious activity.

citation.label: Examination permits and special learner's permits, as amended by P.L.2023, c.216 (effective the first day of the 13th month after the January 8, 2024 approval)

state.reason: New Jersey's graduated licence passenger limit is not defined by passenger age: a permit or probationary licence holder under 21 may carry no more than one passenger of any age, excluding the driver’s dependents, and the limit does not apply when a parent or guardian is in the vehicle.

gdlPassengerPhase1.display: No more than one passenger of any age (dependents of the driver excepted) unless a parent or guardian is in the vehicle; the restriction ends at 21.

citation.label: Examination permits and special learner's permits, as amended by P.L.2023, c.216 (effective the first day of the 13th month after the January 8, 2024 approval)

minLiability.display: For policies issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2026, minimum liability coverage is $35,000 per person / $70,000 per accident for bodily injury and $25,000 for property damage.

citation.label: Maintenance of motor vehicle liability insurance coverage

crashReportThresholdUsd.display: A written crash report must be filed when a crash causes injury, death, or property damage of $500 or more.

citation.label: Immediate notice and written report of accidents, as amended by P.L.2007, c.266 (approved and effective January 13, 2008)

references.label: First driver license and fees
references.citation: NJ MVC - Get your first driver license
